json.summary: A TV reporter stops a random smoking man on the street to ask the classic lottery-jackpot question. While the reporter fires off cliché suggestions (sports car, yacht, villa, and repeatedly 'pussies?'), the man first seems to agree, then reveals an absurdly specific fantasy: buying thousands of size-10 wrenches and scattering them everywhere like dandelion seeds. When the interview escalates, the man morphs into a giant monster and rants about size-6 screws, demanding five of them. The humour lies in the deadpan escalation, the vulgar register, and the total mismatch between the interview format and the insane answer.

characters.name: glasses-wearing reporter with microphone
characters.description: A loud, grinning TV reporter with glasses, unruly hair and a hand-held microphone. He opens with fake-polite greetings ('HÁHHÁ! JÓESTÉT!', 'JÓNAPOT URAM!') and asks the lottery question. In panel p2 he fires off disconnected cliché suggestions, including the repeated vulgar 'PINÁK?' ('pussies?'), which becomes a running gag. Register: sensationalist interviewer, colloquial, not above crude sexual slang.

characters.name: bald man in turtleneck
characters.description: The interviewee: a balding, overweight man in a turtleneck/hoodie, smoking; later drawn as a huge monstrous angry figure in panels p5-p6. He starts calm and thoughtful ('A LOTTÓ ÖTÖST? HM... LÁSSUK CSAK... HEHE... IGEN!'), then gives an absurdly specific answer about buying thousands of size-10 wrenches and scattering them like dandelion seeds, escalating into profane ranting about size-6 screws. Register: casual, clipped, vulgar ('bazmeg', 'kurvanagy', 'szar'), with the verbal tic 'vágod?'/'vagod?' ('get it?').

panels.description: The reporter stands alone, grinning, microphone in hand, and announces that they will wait for the first 'random Tibor' and ask him the question. The bubble is his; no other speaker.
The reporter, microphone out, politely asks the smoking bald man what the first thing he would do if he won the lottery jackpot. The tail runs to the reporter's mouth; the bald man is silent.

The reporter is surrounded by small floating speech fragments with his suggestions ('SPORTKOCSI?', 'PINÁK?', 'YACHT?', 'UTAZGATÁS?', 'PINÁK?', 'VILLA?', 'PINÁK?'). The bald man, smoking, finally speaks/answers with 'A LOTTÓ ÖTÖST? HM... LÁSSUK CSAK... HEHE... IGEN!'; his bubble tail points to him. The repeated 'PINÁK?' is the reporter's running gag.

The bald man gives his real answer: he would buy a huge box full of size-10 wrenches, packed to the brain, several thousand, 'get it?'. The reporter listens with microphone; the speech bubble belongs to the bald man.

The bald man continues his absurd fantasy: wherever the sun turns, he would scatter the wrenches like a dandelion scatters its shits, everywhere. The reporter reacts with a big grin/gesture; the bubble tail points to the bald man.

The bald man suddenly becomes a giant monstrous figure and lunges at the reporter, yelling about a size-6 screw, 'bazmeg'. The reporter cowers and drops his microphone; the jagged bubble belongs to the monstrous interviewee.

The bald man, now sitting/standing over the flattened reporter, finishes his rant: wherever he reaches, it should be there, 'bazmeg', not one, five. The speech bubble is his; the reporter lies on the ground with the dropped microphone.

notes: Napirajz is an absurd, dry Hungarian webcomic; the art is deliberately crude, and the humour depends on dialogue, slang and escalating absurdity. Translators should keep the vulgar register and the deadpan/absurd shifts.
'lottó ötös' = hitting all five numbers in the Hungarian lottery, i.e. the jackpot. Do not translate as 'lottery five' literally; use 'lottery jackpot' or 'winning the lottery'.

'randomtibor' in r0: a compound of 'random' + 'Tibor', a common Hungarian male name, meaning an arbitrary man, like 'random Joe'. It should feel like a TV reporter treating people as specimens. You can adapt the name or keep 'Tibor' with a note.

'PINÁK?' (r4, r8, r11) is the plural of 'pina', a vulgar word for vagina/pussy. The reporter keeps suggesting it as a lottery-winner cliché; the repetition is the gag. Translate as vulgar plural ('Pussies?') and keep all three occurrences.

'SPORTKOCSI?' (r3) = sports car; 'YACHT?' (r6) = yacht, kept English-like; 'UTAZGATÁS?' (r7) = travelling/jaunting; 'VILLA?' (r10) = villa/mansion. These are the reporter's cliché guesses, not the interviewee's words.
r5 'A LOTTÓ ÖTÖST? HM... LÁSSUK CSAK... HEHE... IGEN!' belongs to the interviewee, not the reporter; it is his slow, chuckling realization/answer. 'Lássuk csak' = let's see; 'hehe' is a chuckle.
'vágod?'/'vagod?' (r13, r15) = slang 'you get it?/you dig?/capisce?' It is a verbal tic of the interviewee. Note the dropped accent in r15; it still means the same.
'kurvanagy' (r13) = literally 'whore-big', an obscene intensifier meaning 'fucking big'. Use a strong vulgar equivalent, not a mild one.
'teles-tele' (r13) = reduplicated 'full', 'chock-full/stuffed to the brim'. 'agyig rakva' = literally 'packed to the brain', i.e. completely full; the brain image is part of the absurdity.

'tizes villáskulcs' (r13) = a size-10 open-end wrench. Keep the metric size: 'size-10 wrench/spanner'. The precision matters because it clashes with the huge quantity ('több ezer' = several thousand).

'pitypang a szarjait' (r15): 'pitypang' = dandelion; 'szarjait' = its shits. The simile is deliberately vulgar and absurd: he would scatter wrenches like a dandelion scatters its crap. Keep the crude image.
'hatos csavar' (r16) = a size-6 screw/bolt, not 'six screws'. The joke depends on the obsessive tool sizes; translating it as 'six screws' would kill the specificity.
'bazmeg' (r16, r17) = contraction of 'baszd meg', a strong swear meaning 'fuck'. It should be translated with equivalent profanity; it marks the interviewee's shift from calm to aggressive.
'HOGYAMIKOR' (r16) = collapsed 'hogy amikor', very colloquial; it signals uneducated/casual speech. In English, use contracted/dropped grammar to match ('whenever there's...' etc.).
'NEM EGY, ÖT!' (r17) = literally 'not one, five!' The clipped syntax is a punchline: he wants not one but five size-6 screws/bolts. Keep it terse and slightly ungrammatical.

The reporter's fake politeness in r0/r2 ('JÓESTÉT!', 'JÓNAPOT URAM!') contrasts with his crude suggestions; the interviewee's first polite 'IGEN' contrasts with his later monstrous rant. The comedy is the sudden escalation.

Panel p5-p6 visual gag: the interviewee turns into a giant monster, but he is still the same bald man in a turtleneck. The dialogue must stay in the same voice, just louder/angrier; do not assign these lines to a new character.
The repeated 'PINÁK?' and 'vágod?' are running verbal tics; preserve them consistently across panels.
No background signs or brand names in the supplied panels; the red numbered boxes are localization aids, not part of the comic.
